source: Astra Migrate Product Backlog v1.0 (17 Nov 2026), spec v1.1

stories.story: As a platform administrator, I want to create a separate tenant for each customer estate with its own storage, compute and encryption keys, so that customer data can never mix between customers or partners.
acceptance: Each tenant has its own storage and its own encryption keys.
An automated test proves that a query from one tenant cannot read another tenant's data.
Tenant creation and deletion are written to the audit log.
stories.note: DB per tenant + role + non-exportable key; isolation proven in tests/test_tenancy.py

stories.story: As a platform administrator, I want to choose the hosting region when I create a tenant, so that data residency rules in the blueprint are met.
acceptance: The region is fixed at creation and can only change through a recorded migration task.
Model calls use endpoints in the same region where the provider offers them.
A blueprint residency control blocks a project in a non-compliant region.
stories.note: Region fixed at creation (DB-enforced), recorded region moves, and blueprint residency controls block projects in non-compliant regions or without in-region model endpoints.

stories.story: As a platform administrator, I want to deploy the platform into a customer's own Azure or AWS account, so that regulated customers can keep all data inside their own cloud.
acceptance: Infrastructure-as-code templates exist for Azure and AWS.
A deployment guide and automated smoke tests are provided.
A customer-account deployment passes the same security tests as the shared service.

stories.story: As a platform user, I want to sign in with my company's single sign-on and multi-factor authentication, so that I do not need a separate password for the platform.
acceptance: Microsoft Entra ID and Okta work through SAML or OpenID Connect.
Multi-factor authentication is enforced by tenant policy.
Session timeout can be set per tenant.
stories.note: Generic multi-issuer OIDC, tenant MFA policy (amr) and per-tenant session timeout done and tested with Keycloak. Remaining: verify against a real Microsoft Entra ID and Okta tenant.

stories.story: As a platform administrator, I want to assign roles to users per programme, partner and project, so that each person sees and does only what their role allows.
acceptance: Roles include all roles listed in this backlog.
A partner user can see only the customers assigned to that partner.
Every role change is written to the audit log.
stories.note: All backlog roles; programme/partner/tenant scopes; partner isolation and audited grants tested

stories.story: As a platform administrator, I want to store connector credentials as secrets in a vault, so that passwords never appear in blueprints, logs or screens.
acceptance: Secrets are read only at run time by the connector that needs them.
Secrets can be rotated without changing the blueprint.
A log scan in the test suite finds no secret values.
stories.note: Vault-held connector secrets, secret:// references, rotation, audited run-time reads, log scan test

stories.story: As an auditor, I want to have every user action and agent action written to a write-once audit log, so that I can prove who did what and when.
acceptance: Log entries cannot be changed or deleted by any user, including administrators.
Entries are hash-chained so tampering can be detected.
The log can be filtered by project, person, agent and time and exported.
stories.note: Privileges + triggers + hash chain + vault-signed anchors; filter and CSV/JSONL export

stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want to trace every agent call, tool call and load step with its duration and cost, so that I can find slow or expensive steps and report cost per stage.
acceptance: Traces use OpenTelemetry.
A dashboard shows time and model cost per project, stage and agent.
A trace can be opened from any review item.
stories.note: Model cost per agent and per model on the dashboard (I3). Remaining: open trace from review items (I8).

stories.story: As a customer IT security lead, I want to stream the audit log to my own security monitoring tool, so that the migration is covered by our normal security monitoring.
acceptance: Export works to at least Microsoft Sentinel and Splunk.
Export delay is under five minutes.
Failed exports raise an alert.

stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want to register each agent with its role, allowed tools, guardrails and test suite on the Astra Data Factory runtime, so that agents behave in a controlled and repeatable way.
acceptance: An agent cannot call a tool outside its registered list.
Each project is pinned to agent versions.
An agent release is blocked if its test suite fails.
stories.note: Agent registry with own identities, closed tool catalogue, project pins and suite-gated release (released versions immutable in the database). Model cases stay Blocked until a model key is configured.

stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want to call models through one model-neutral gateway with Claude as the default, so that we can change models without changing agents.
acceptance: The gateway supports at least two model providers.
Models are called through enterprise endpoints with no training on customer data.
Each call records the model name and version.
stories.note: Gateway with aliases; drivers for Anthropic (default), Claude on Foundry and Azure OpenAI; refuses providers without credential, no-training terms or region; every call recorded (served model, API version, tokens, cost). Azure drivers not yet called live (no keys).

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to have an Orchestrator agent plan stages, assign tasks to agents and ask people for decisions, so that work moves forward without manual hand-offs.
acceptance: The Orchestrator can read status and metadata but not business data values.
Every decision it requests appears in the review queue with an owner.
Stage status is visible on the project dashboard.
stories.note: Orchestrator (metadata-only tools), review queue with owner role/user, stage strip with deterministic gates. Running it needs a configured model provider.

stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want to pass all text found in legacy data to agents as data, never as instructions, so that text such as a policy note cannot change agent behaviour.
acceptance: Free-text fields are wrapped and labelled as data in every agent call.
A screening step flags instruction-like content for review.
The guardrail test suite includes at least 20 manipulation cases, and all pass.
stories.note: Escaped, labelled untrusted_data wrapping, data policy in every prompt, deterministic screening into the review queue; 32 manipulation and 12 benign cases pass.

stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want to enforce hard rules outside the model, so that no agent can write to a target database, approve its own proposal or skip a gate.
acceptance: Tool permissions make direct target database writes impossible.
An agent identity can never be the approver of any item.
Gate checks run in deterministic code.
stories.note: No target-write/approve/publish tools exist; database triggers refuse agent identities as any decider; gates in code.

stories.story: As an auditor, I want to see a governance record for every agent with its purpose, risk rating, oversight rules and test history, so that I can explain to regulators how migration decisions were made.
acceptance: A record exists for every registered agent version.
The record links to the latest test results.
Records are included in the proof pack.
stories.note: Governance record per agent version (purpose, risk, oversight, hard rules, tools, models, test history). Inclusion in the proof pack lands with I11.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to create a Migration Blueprint in a form or as a YAML file, so that I can set up a migration without writing code.
acceptance: The form and the file stay in sync.
Blueprints are stored in Git with full history.
A new blueprint can be copied from a template.
stories.note: Form and YAML views over one canonical model, git history per tenant, templates.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to compare two versions of a blueprint, so that I can see exactly what changed between plans.
acceptance: The comparison shows added, removed and changed fields.
Each version shows who changed it and why.
stories.note: Structural diff (added/removed/changed) with author and reason per version.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to get help from a Blueprint Assistant that asks questions and suggests packs, so that a new migration lead can set up a blueprint correctly.
acceptance: The assistant suggests source, target, domain and compliance packs from my answers.
Every suggestion shows its reason.
Nothing is saved until I accept it.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to check a blueprint for missing fields and incompatible packs, so that problems are found before planning starts.
acceptance: Every problem is explained in plain language with a fix.
Planning cannot start while blocking problems remain.
stories.note: Plain-language issues with fixes; planning gate refuses while blocking problems remain.

stories.story: As a compliance curator, I want to see every rule conflict between packs, so that a person decides each conflict and no default is applied silently.
acceptance: Conflicts list both rules and their sources.
A decision records the person, time and reason.
stories.note: Conflicts list both values and source packs; decisions record person, time and reason; no default applied.

stories.story: As a compliance curator, I want to require a named approver and a reason before any compliance rule is loosened, so that weaker controls are always deliberate.
acceptance: Loosening is blocked without approval.
The approval appears in the proof pack.
stories.note: Loosening blocked until a different, named approver approves with a reason. Remaining: include approvals in the proof pack (I11).

stories.story: As a customer data owner, I want to approve a blueprint version together with the migration lead, so that planning starts from a configuration both sides agree on.
acceptance: An approved version is locked.
Changes after approval create a new version that needs approval again.
stories.note: Dual approval by required roles; approved versions locked in the database; changes create a new version needing approval.

stories.story: As an ontology and pack curator, I want to publish a pack with a version, its contents, its tests and a status, so that projects use only tested packs.
acceptance: A pack cannot be published if its tests fail.
Published versions are immutable.
Each project records the exact pack versions it uses.
stories.note: Draft -> tests -> publish; publish refused when tests fail; published versions immutable in the database; blueprints pin exact versions.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to upgrade a project to a newer pack version on purpose, so that projects never change behaviour without a decision.
acceptance: Upgrades show what changes in the plan before they are applied.
An upgrade needs migration lead approval.
stories.note: Pack version diff done; upgrading a pin is a new blueprint version that needs approval. Remaining: show plan impact of an upgrade (needs the planner, I7).

stories.story: As a compliance curator, I want to have packs declare what they need and what they add, so that the platform can combine packs safely.
acceptance: A pack can add controls but never remove controls added by another pack.
When two packs set different values, the stricter one is shown and a person confirms it.
stories.note: Packs declare requires/adds; schema has no removal; conflicts show the stricter value and need a recorded decision.

stories.story: As a pack developer, I want to build a new adapter or pack with templates, a local test kit and documentation, so that partners can extend the platform without Artizent engineers.
acceptance: The SDK includes templates for each pack type.
The local test kit runs the same checks as the registry.
Published partner packs need curator approval.

stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want to define one adapter contract for connect, read metadata, extract data, read code, list known traps, load data and report limits, so that every product plugs into the platform in the same way.
acceptance: The contract is documented and versioned.
A contract test suite checks any adapter.
Adapters run with read-only access to sources.
stories.note: Contract astra.adapters/v1 documented (docs/adapter-contract.md) and versioned; contract checks at registration; golden datasets act as the contract test suite; read-only guard, account check and rolled-back sessions.

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to connect to a ConceptOne database on SAP SQL Anywhere or Microsoft SQL Server with read-only access, so that discovery can start without risk to the live system.
acceptance: Both database engines are supported.
The connection uses a read-only account.
Connection checks report the engine and version.
stories.note: SQL Server proven read-only with engine and version reported. SQL Anywhere driver written; Blocked until an engine with SAP client libraries is available.

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to read ConceptOne metadata, including user-defined tables, procedures, triggers, validation, workflows, security profiles and External Programs settings, so that the knowledge graph covers the whole estate.
acceptance: Every object type in the list is read.
Each object records its owner, last change date where available, and dependencies.
A coverage report shows any object that could not be read.
stories.note: All listed object types read with owner, last change and dependencies, plus a coverage report; proven on the synthetic estate. Re-prove on a real estate (adapter marked unvalidated).

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to extract ConceptOne data and File Cabinet documents with their entity links, so that data and documents can be moved together.
acceptance: Extraction can run in full and as deltas.
Document metadata keeps the link to its policy, claim or party.
Extract counts are recorded for reconciliation.
stories.note: Full and delta extraction, File Cabinet documents with entity links, counts checked against the source; data kept in the tenant database.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to keep a list of known ConceptOne traps in the adapter, so that each project avoids problems found in earlier projects.
acceptance: Traps can be added by curators.
Discovery flags any trap that applies to an estate.
stories.note: Traps ship in the adapter pack and curators add more (API); harvests flag every trap that applies.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to load the Pro Suite Base baseline metadata provided by Insurity, so that the version delta engine has a target to compare against.
acceptance: Baseline versions are stored and named.
A project is pinned to one baseline version.
stories.note: Baselines stored by name, immutable, pinned per project. Only a synthetic baseline exists until Insurity provides the real one.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to load data only through Insurity-approved tools and the Pro Suite REST APIs with OAuth2, so that the platform respects the vendor's rules for a hosted tenant.
acceptance: No direct database writes are possible.
API rate limits are respected and recorded.
Each load call is logged with its result.
stories.note: REST/OAuth2 loader with rate limiting and every call logged; no database load method exists. Pro Suite endpoints unknown, so reference loads are Blocked.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to record Pro Suite constraints in the adapter, such as PDF-only forms, retired workflow objects, tenant provisioning lead time and change windows, so that the planner and designers work within real limits.
acceptance: Each constraint has a source and a date.
Constraints appear as rules in planning and design.
stories.note: Constraints carry source, date and confidence and compose as TGT- planning rules.

stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want to build adapters for further products such as IBM Maximo, SAP PM, IFS Cloud and other policy systems, so that the platform can take on cross-product migrations.
acceptance: Each adapter passes the contract test suite.
Each adapter passes its own golden dataset.

stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want to offer an ontology service with five operations: find concept, get concept, get constraints, get vendor binding and get precedents, so that agents use the ontology without loading it whole.
acceptance: The service uses a graph store and a vector index.
Each answer records the ontology version.
Response time stays under one second for 95 percent of calls.
stories.note: Five operations over a Postgres property graph and pgvector HNSW index; every answer names its ontology version; p95 well under 1 s in tests. Embeddings are lexical until a model embedder is added.

stories.story: As an ontology and pack curator, I want to maintain a core ontology of shared business concepts such as party, product, contract, transaction, document and obligation, so that industry packs build on one shared base.
acceptance: Concepts have definitions, synonyms and relations.
The core is versioned and tested.
stories.note: core-ontology@1.0.0: concepts with definitions, synonyms and relations; validated and tested.

stories.story: As an ontology and pack curator, I want to publish a property and casualty pack with the MGA and delegated authority extension, so that agents understand policies, billing, bordereaux, multi-carrier splits, premium finance, surplus lines taxes and commissions.
acceptance: Each concept in the extension table of the spec exists with rules.
Rules state that premium, taxes, fees and commissions must reconcile to the cent.
The pack passes the ConceptOne golden dataset.
stories.note: pc-insurance@1.0.0 with the MGA extension; reconcile-to-the-cent rules; passes the golden dataset.

stories.story: As an ontology and pack curator, I want to review proposals for ontology changes from projects, so that the ontology improves without losing quality.
acceptance: Proposals arrive anonymised with their evidence.
Only a curator can accept a change.
A new version must pass the golden datasets before release.

stories.story: As an ontology and pack curator, I want to build further domain packs such as banking, wealth, industrial assets and healthcare, so that the platform can serve more industries.
acceptance: Each pack lists the standards it uses.
Each pack has its own golden dataset.

stories.story: As a compliance curator, I want to define controls as one of six types: data handling, approval, gate, evidence, residency and retention, so that the planner knows where each control belongs.
acceptance: Each type has a placement rule in the planner.
Every placed control appears in the control matrix.
stories.note: Six control types with placement rules, validated per type. Remaining: control matrix in the plan (I7).

stories.story: As a compliance curator, I want to publish packs for SOX and IT general controls, SOC 1, the NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law, state insurance record retention and state surplus lines filing, so that the ConceptOne reference case carries its obligations into the plan.
acceptance: Each pack lists its controls with sources.
Each control states the evidence that proves it.
Packs are reviewed by a named compliance specialist before release.
stories.note: Five packs with sourced controls and evidence pass their tests; publication waits for a named compliance specialist's review.

stories.story: As a compliance curator, I want to publish a Lloyd's delegated authority pack, so that coverholder customers can show their obligations are met.
acceptance: Coverholder reporting and binding authority records are covered.

stories.story: As a compliance curator, I want to publish further packs such as GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, DORA, 21 CFR Part 11 and the EU AI Act, so that the platform can serve other regulated industries.
acceptance: Each pack follows the same control types.
Each pack states clearly that it supports but does not certify compliance.

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to harvest source and target data dictionaries, so that every element is known before design starts.
acceptance: Tables, fields, types, relations and code lists are read.
Harvest results are stored in the knowledge graph.
stories.note: Tables, columns, types, foreign keys, soft references and code lists harvested into the knowledge graph; target tables from the pinned baseline (same-name candidates until I6).

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to profile every in-scope table, so that data quality problems are known early.
acceptance: The profile shows null rates, distinct counts, patterns and broken references.
A data quality score is calculated per table and per estate.
stories.note: Null rates, distinct counts, value shapes and broken references per table; quality score per table and estate with published weights.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to measure how often each element is used, so that unused items can be retired instead of migrated.
acceptance: Usage covers at least the last 90 days where logs allow.
Elements with no use are flagged for retirement review.
stories.note: Usage from imported login and query records over a 90-day window, flowing through code and triggers; unused elements flagged for retirement review in the review queue.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to read stored procedures, triggers, scripts and External Programs with the Astra RE Harness, so that business rules hidden in code are found.
acceptance: Each rule found is linked to the fields and screens it affects.
Rules are listed with a confidence score and the code excerpt.
stories.note: Static code reader: rules with kind, confidence, excerpt and fields (read and set). Screens link when an adapter supplies screen metadata; the Astra RE Harness is not integrated.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to find every interface and program that connects to the legacy database, so that no hidden integration breaks at cutover.
acceptance: Connections are found from database login records and query logs.
Each interface records its source, frequency and the objects it touches.
stories.note: Interfaces from login records and query logs, linked-server code and interface objects, each with source, frequency and objects touched.

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to read configuration such as books, products, rating, forms, rules and workflows, so that configuration can be carried over and compared.
acceptance: Each configuration item is stored with its dependencies.
Configuration differences between books are shown.
stories.note: Configuration items per kind with dependencies; differences between books shown.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to rebuild real workflows from audit logs and workflow history, so that agentification candidates are based on how work is really done.
acceptance: Workflows are shown as steps with volumes and times.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to see a discovery coverage report for the knowledge graph, so that I know discovery is complete before planning.
acceptance: The report shows coverage per stream and lists gaps.
Gate approval for discovery needs this report.
stories.note: Coverage report across nine streams with gaps; waivers and acceptance by people; the discovery stage gate needs an accepted report.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to compare a customer's database and configuration with the target baseline, object by object, so that only real differences need design work.
acceptance: Differences are sorted into unchanged, renamed or moved, changed behaviour, and removed in target.
The same inputs always give the same result.
Results can be exported for review.
stories.note: Deterministic four-group delta with digests; CSV/JSON export (platform/src/astra_migrate/delta).

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to see which differences are customer-specific and which come from the product version, so that effort is spent where it is needed.
acceptance: Each difference shows whether it matches the standard version or is a customization.
stories.note: Origin from the source product's standard baseline, or the adapter's customization flag; otherwise unknown.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to set the migration pattern in the blueprint and see the planner's view on it, so that the fastest safe approach is chosen.
acceptance: Patterns are cross-product, same-family upgrade and consolidation.
The planner can propose another pattern with reasons.
stories.note: Pattern advice with evidence; disagreement with the blueprint becomes a review proposal.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to map cross-product migrations through the domain ontology, so that the platform can move data between unrelated products.
acceptance: Mappings link source element, concept and target element.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to convert procedures, triggers, views, data types, identity columns and date functions from SAP SQL Anywhere to Microsoft SQL Server, so that ConceptOne customizations run on the target database.
acceptance: Each converted object compiles on SQL Server.
Objects that cannot be converted automatically go to the review queue with a reason.
stories.note: Rule-based SQL Anywhere to SQL Server converter, compiled on a rolled-back SQL Server workbench; review with reason otherwise. Reading code from a live SQL Anywhere estate waits for an engine.

stories.story: As a test engineer, I want to test converted objects with recorded inputs and outputs from the source, so that I can prove they behave the same.
acceptance: Each object has at least one recorded test case.
Differences are listed with their inputs.
stories.note: Recorded cases replayed on the workbench; differences listed with their inputs.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to convert further engine pairs, such as Sybase ASE or Oracle to SQL Server or PostgreSQL, so that other legacy products can be moved.
acceptance: Each pair has its own test suite.

stories.story: As a customer IT security lead, I want to get a checklist for network, identity and security set-up for the move to a hosted tenant, so that users can reach the new system on day one.
acceptance: The checklist covers single sign-on, MFA, network access and printing.
Each item has an owner and status in the plan.
stories.note: Hosting checklist from target adapter constraints plus the four required areas; owners and statuses.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to have the Scope Analyst decide what happens to each legacy element, with evidence, so that scope is complete and explainable.
acceptance: Every element ends as migrate, rebuild, replace with standard, agentify, archive or retire.
Each decision shows its evidence and needs approval.
stories.note: Scope register: rule-based proposals with evidence for all six dispositions; people approve or change them with a reason. The Scope Analyst agent needs a model key.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to see a dependency graph across all nine streams, so that work happens in the right order.
acceptance: Dependencies can be viewed and edited.
Cycles are reported as errors.
stories.note: Dependency graph from the knowledge graph across streams; people add and remove edges; cycles are errors.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to get a work breakdown in which no task is longer than 40 hours, so that every task can be tracked.
acceptance: Tasks over 40 hours are split automatically.
Each task has an owner role and dependencies.
stories.note: Tasks per activity of pack estimation rules, split to the blueprint's maximum (40 h), with owner roles and dependencies.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to see estimates as ranges with the evidence behind them, so that I understand how confident each estimate is.
acceptance: Each range shows the pack rules and past tasks used.
Totals roll up by stream, segment and wave.
stories.note: Ranges with the rule, pack and past tasks used; roll-ups by stream, segment, wave and role.

stories.story: As a compliance curator, I want to see a control matrix built from the selected compliance packs, so that every control has a task and evidence.
acceptance: Each control links to the tasks and gates where it applies.
stories.note: Control matrix from the blueprint's compliance packs: control task, governed tasks and gates.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to group work into waves and have the constraint solver check them, so that the plan fits capacity, windows and freeze periods.
acceptance: The solver reports every broken constraint.
When the plan does not fit, options are offered and no work is dropped silently.
stories.note: OR-Tools CP-SAT wave solver: every broken constraint and the options; no work dropped.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to keep a risk register with likelihood, impact, owner and a mitigation task, so that risks are managed inside the plan.
acceptance: New risks found by agents need a person to accept them.
stories.note: Risk register; planner-found risks are proposals a person accepts.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to compare whole-estate, phased and parallel-run cutover for a customer, so that the cutover strategy is chosen on evidence.
acceptance: The comparison shows duration, effort, risk and constraints for each option.
The chosen option and its reason are recorded.
stories.note: Whole-estate, phased and parallel-run compared on duration, effort, risk and constraints; choice recorded with its reason.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to get a timed cutover runbook with go/no-go checks and a rollback plan, so that cutover runs the same way it was rehearsed.
acceptance: Each step has an owner and a planned duration.
Rehearsal timings update the runbook.
stories.note: Timed runbook with go/no-go checks and rollback; rehearsal timings update it.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to approve a plan baseline and see every later change with its reason, so that changes are controlled.
acceptance: Each re-plan shows a diff against the baseline.
Changes to an approved baseline need approval.
stories.note: Plan baselines approved by a second person; re-plans diffed against the approved baseline.

stories.story: As a partner delivery lead, I want to export the plan to Jira and Azure DevOps, so that teams work in their usual tools.
acceptance: Export keeps task IDs so updates sync back.
Actual effort flows back into the platform.
stories.note: Jira and Azure DevOps CSV exports with stable task ids; actual effort imported back and used for calibration. Live API sync needs credentials.

stories.story: As a partner delivery lead, I want to export the plan to Microsoft Project, so that managers who use it can follow the plan.
acceptance: Dependencies and dates are kept.

stories.story: As a sales engineer, I want to produce a pre-sales estimate from a questionnaire and a sample extract, so that proposals are based on data, not guesses.
acceptance: The output is clearly marked as an estimate.
It shows a scope outline, waves and an effort range.
stories.note: Pre-sales estimate from a questionnaire and an optional sample extract, labelled as an estimate with every assumption.

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to receive mapping proposals with evidence and a confidence score, so that I can review them quickly.
acceptance: Each proposal lists its evidence and precedents.
Low-confidence items go to expert review.
stories.note: Mapping proposals with evidence, precedents and a documented confidence; below 0.8 and no-target columns go to the data SME in the review queue, whose decision updates the register.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to have the Configuration Translator rebuild books, products, rating, rules and workflows in the target, so that configuration moves without manual re-keying.
acceptance: Each item records its source and target.
Workflow objects retired in the target are flagged with a proposed replacement.
stories.note: Configuration items record source and target area, key, method and translated definition; retirements from the target adapter are flagged with the proposed replacement. Applying to the target happens with loads (I10).

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to convert forms to the target's PDF-only format, so that documents still generate correctly.
acceptance: Each converted form is compared with its golden copy in parity testing.
stories.note: Forms are approved only after the converted PDF passes parity (pages, sizes, text, fields) against the approved golden copy.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to have the Code Modernizer re-create user-defined tables, procedures and validation to the target's standards, so that customizations are supported after migration.
acceptance: Generated code follows the target naming and ownership rules.
Each item has tests and passes before it can be deployed.
stories.note: Customer tables and converted code renamed by the target's naming rules; generated code is tested on the SQL Server workbench (compile, key, recorded cases, at least one) and approved per version.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to replace direct database calls with REST API, DBQuery or webhook calls, so that integrations work on the hosted tenant.
acceptance: Each interface found in discovery has a target design.
Each rebuilt interface has an end-to-end test.
stories.note: Each discovered interface gets a target design on an approved mechanism by direction; approval needs an end-to-end test definition, run against a target connection.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to replace External Programs and Outlook COM integrations, so that desktop-only links keep working for browser users.
acceptance: Each one has a target design or an approved retirement.
stories.note: Desktop-only links matching a target retirement go to review: approved retirement or browser replacement.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to rebuild reports and extracts on approved access such as DBQuery procedures, so that reports work without direct database reads.
acceptance: Each rebuilt report passes report parity.
stories.note: Views rebuilt as read-only procedures on the report access mechanism with mapped names, compiled and run on the workbench. Report parity runs with validation (I10).

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to draft UX Designer web layouts from ConceptOne screens and extend security profiles, so that business users get usable web screens.
acceptance: Drafts need designer approval.
Every user role has the new objects in its security profile.
stories.note: Page drafts per entity from its mappings need designer approval; every security profile needs an access decision for every new object before approval. Legacy screen layouts need adapter metadata.

stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want to generate data transformation code and unit tests with Astra Data from approved mappings, so that data moves by tested code, not by agents.
acceptance: Code is versioned.
Code cannot run until its tests pass.
stories.note: Transformation procedures from approved mappings, versioned by digest, tested on SQL Server with real extract rows and edge rows; only approved versions whose tests passed can run (database).

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to run each load as a numbered run with fixed code, pack and input versions, so that any run can be repeated exactly.
acceptance: A rerun with the same versions gives the same result.
Each run records counts and errors.

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to see records that failed to load in an error queue with the target's reason, so that failures are fixed and reloaded.
acceptance: Errors can be filtered and assigned.
Fixed records can be reloaded alone.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to load by segment, such as line of business or region, and apply delta loads before cutover, so that large estates can move in waves.
acceptance: Delta loads include only changes since the last run.

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to size document volume by type and age, so that load time and storage can be planned.
acceptance: Sizing appears in discovery results and the plan.
stories.note: Documents sized by type, age and entity in discovery results; appears in the plan with I7.

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to check every document link after migration and test a random sample byte for byte, so that users can open every document.
acceptance: Broken links are listed with their entity.
The sample size is set in the blueprint.

stories.story: As a test engineer, I want to run structural, reference, semantic and business rules after each transformation and load, so that errors are found before cutover.
acceptance: Each failure explains the rule, the record and a proposed fix in plain language.

stories.story: As a customer data owner, I want to reconcile counts, premium, taxes, fees, commissions, open items and ledger balances to the cent, so that I can sign off that nothing was lost.
acceptance: Reconciliation runs after every load.
Every break has an owner until it is closed.

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to see a data quality score before and after migration, so that improvements are visible.
acceptance: Scores are shown per object and per segment.

stories.story: As a test engineer, I want to re-rate a sample of policies in both systems and explain every premium difference, so that rating behaves the same after migration.
acceptance: Differences show inputs and both outputs.
Each approved difference records its approver.

stories.story: As a test engineer, I want to compare generated forms with approved golden copies, so that documents sent to customers are correct.
acceptance: Content differences fail the test.
Layout-only differences need approval.

stories.story: As a test engineer, I want to compare key reports and workflow outcomes between source and target, so that operations and finance can trust the new system.
acceptance: Report totals must match to the cent.
Workflow replays compare tasks, routing and outcomes.

stories.story: As a customer data owner, I want to close one accounting period in both systems during a parallel run, so that finance signs off the move.
acceptance: Ledger, receivables, payables and commissions are compared.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to name a system of record for every shared entity in every phase, so that everyone knows which system owns which data.
acceptance: A phased plan cannot be approved without these rules.
stories.note: Coexistence rules per shared entity per phase; phased plans cannot be approved without them.

stories.story: As a customer data owner, I want to reconcile shared entities and accounting balances across both systems every day, so that breaks are found within a day.
acceptance: Breaks go to a named owner.
The coexistence dashboard shows open breaks.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to set an end date and exit reconciliation for every coexistence period, so that coexistence does not run on without control.
acceptance: The planner warns when an end date is at risk.
stories.note: End dates and exit reconciliation per coexistence period, with at-risk warnings.

stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want to synchronise shared entities one way or both ways with named conflict rules, so that users can work in both systems during the phase.
acceptance: Every sync action is logged.
Conflicts follow the configured rule or go to review.

stories.story: As a reviewer, I want to work from a queue sorted by risk, confidence and compliance impact, so that I spend time where it matters.
acceptance: Filters exist for stream, segment and agent.
stories.note: Queue sorted by a documented priority (risk, compliance impact, confidence) with filters for stream, segment, agent, kind, risk, compliance, owner role and 'mine'; facets and pattern groups.

stories.story: As a reviewer, I want to see the evidence, sample values and precedents for each item, so that I can decide in seconds.
acceptance: Evidence links open the source object.
stories.note: Evidence panel: evidence links to the source objects, sample values read from the tenant at view time, an explanation from the recorded evidence and precedents.

stories.story: As a reviewer, I want to approve, reject with a reason or change an item, so that my decision drives the next step.
acceptance: A change goes back to the agent with my note.
Compliance-critical items need a named reviewer, and two people where a pack requires it.
stories.note: Approve, reject with a reason or change; a change starts a follow-up run of the requesting agent with the note. Compliance-critical items need a named reviewer and two people where a pack requires it (database triggers).

stories.story: As a reviewer, I want to ask the Review Assistant why an item was proposed, so that I understand it before deciding.
acceptance: The assistant cannot approve anything.
stories.note: Review Assistant agent with two metadata-read tools and no deciding tool. Needs a pinned release and a model key to answer; the recorded-evidence explanation is always shown.

stories.story: As a reviewer, I want to approve similar items in bulk when they share the same evidence pattern, so that large reviews take less time.
acceptance: Bulk approval is not allowed for compliance-critical items.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to view and edit the plan as a timeline, a task list and a dependency graph, so that I can manage the plan in one place.
acceptance: Edits trigger the constraint solver.
The screens meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
stories.note: Planning workbench view (timeline, task list, graph) and batched edits that re-run the CP-SAT solver; task changes survive regeneration.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to manage gates with checklists, such as G0 to G4 in the reference case, so that no stage closes without its evidence.
acceptance: Each gate lists required evidence and approvers.
Compliance packs can add gate conditions.

stories.story: As an auditor, I want to get a proof pack per wave and per project with configuration, scope, lineage, decisions, controls, tests, agent records, cutover and decommission evidence, so that I can audit the migration without asking the team.
acceptance: The pack is produced as a signed PDF and as structured data.
Every item links back to its source record.

stories.story: As a programme owner at the product company, I want to set up a programme with its source product, target product, partners and customers, so that all migrations share one playbook and one set of packs.
acceptance: Each customer is assigned to one partner.
Partners see only their own customers.

stories.story: As a sales engineer, I want to run a light scan on each consenting customer's estate that reads only metadata and statistics, so that we can size the whole installed base before contracts.
acceptance: No business data values are read.
Customer consent is recorded before a scan.

stories.story: As a commercial manager, I want to see a Migration Complexity Index and band for each customer and segment, so that prices and plans are based on measured complexity.
acceptance: Each score shows the measures and weights behind it.
Bands are simple, medium or complex.

stories.story: As a commercial manager, I want to recalibrate the index weights from actual effort after each wave, so that bands become more accurate over time.
acceptance: Each weights version is stored and dated.
Bands already contracted do not change.

stories.story: As a programme owner at the product company, I want to schedule customers across waves within partner and pod capacity, so that the programme finishes on time.
acceptance: Pod rotation between customers is planned.
Capacity conflicts are reported.

stories.story: As a programme owner at the product company, I want to see one dashboard across all customers and partners, so that I know the state of the whole programme.
acceptance: It shows band, gate status, risks, open vendor gaps and reconciliation results.
Customer data is never shown across partners.

stories.story: As a commercial manager, I want to record bands, gate evidence, effort and elapsed time for each customer and segment, so that milestone billing and the productivity dividend follow evidence.
acceptance: Gate evidence can be exported for invoicing.
Effort per segment is compared across waves.

stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to route every gap to configuration, customer extension, vendor product change or process change, so that each gap has the right owner.
acceptance: A gap cannot close without a route and an owner.
stories.note: Gaps routed to configuration, customer extension, vendor product change or process change; no close without a route and an owner (API and database).

stories.story: As a programme owner at the product company, I want to see vendor product changes as plan dependencies with the customers and waves they block, so that product changes are ranked by the migrations they unblock.
acceptance: The ranked list can be exported for the vendor's product team.
stories.note: Vendor product changes as wave dependencies, ranked across a programme's customers; CSV export.

stories.epic_name: Agentification and Digital Worker test range
stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to rank agentification candidates by volume, effort, rule clarity, data, risk and value, so that we build the Digital Workers that pay back first.
acceptance: Each score shows its evidence.

stories.epic_name: Agentification and Digital Worker test range
stories.story: As a solution architect, I want to design a Digital Worker with an outcome contract, hard guardrails, an autonomy level and an AI risk record, so that every worker is safe by design.
acceptance: A design cannot be approved without all four parts.

stories.epic_name: Agentification and Digital Worker test range
stories.story: As a test engineer, I want to run each Digital Worker through scenario tests, including manipulation and safety cases, so that only certified workers reach production.
acceptance: Release is blocked without a test range certificate.

stories.epic_name: Agentification and Digital Worker test range
stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want to deploy Digital Workers to Astra Agents or to the target product's own agent studio, so that workers run where the customer needs them.
acceptance: Deployment target is set in the design.

stories.epic_name: Agentification and Digital Worker test range
stories.story: As an operations manager at the customer, I want to monitor Digital Workers in production and roll back to a lower autonomy level, so that problems are contained quickly.
acceptance: Drift alerts go to a named owner.
Rollback takes effect within minutes.

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to see precedents from earlier decisions in my tenant when I review, so that decisions stay consistent.
acceptance: Precedents show their source project and outcome.
stories.note: Precedents by pattern key within the tenant, with source project, outcome, answer and who decided.

stories.story: As an ontology and pack curator, I want to promote anonymised patterns to shared memory only when the customer contract allows it, so that learning is shared without exposing customer data.
acceptance: Sharing is off by default.
A person checks a sample of each anonymised batch.

stories.story: As a data subject expert, I want to approve project skills drafted from repeated corrections or errors, so that agents stop repeating the same mistakes.
acceptance: Skills cannot change guardrails or compliance rules.
Each agent call records the skills it used.

stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want to send high-volume, fixed-option questions to a fast decision model with caching, so that row-level tagging is affordable.
acceptance: Each decision is cached by input, question and pack version.
Low-confidence answers go to the reasoning model, then to a person.

stories.story: As a migration lead, I want to have estimates improve from actual effort on past tasks, so that plans get more accurate over time.
acceptance: Estimate error is reported per wave.

stories.story: As a test engineer, I want to build a synthetic ConceptOne golden dataset with known correct outcomes, so that the first release can be measured from the start.
acceptance: The dataset includes seeded errors, hidden rules and interfaces.
stories.note: Synthetic golden estate with seeded errors, hidden rules and interfaces; runner scores every measure; pack tests require a passing golden run.

stories.story: As a test engineer, I want to block a release if any measure drops below the previous release on any golden dataset, so that quality never goes backwards.
acceptance: Measures cover mapping, configuration, code, planning, compliance and review.

stories.story: As a test engineer, I want to measure how well confidence scores match reviewer outcomes, so that review thresholds can be trusted.
acceptance: Calibration error is reported per agent.
